Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:10:1.hebrew: משכחת לה לקולא - דהויא לה הגאולה קולא גביה, לטובתו, ומשכחת לה לרעתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:10:1.english: You find it [with] leniency - For the redemption has a leniency with regard to him, to his benefit; and you also find it to his detriment.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:10:2.hebrew: זבניה במאה - קנאו במנה, ויהיב ליה האי עבד בתר הכי חמשים בגאולת חציו. אי אמרת הויא גאולה — כי אייקר, תו לא ברשות דמריה אייקר, אלא פלגיה. ואם בא עכשיו לגמור פדיונו, יהיב ליה מאה ונפיק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:10:2.english: He purchased him for one hundred - He acquired him for a maneh, and afterward this slave gave him fifty for the redemption of half of him. If you say that this is a [valid] redemption — when [the slave] increased in value, he increased in value no longer in the possession of his master, but only [as to] his [remaining] half. And if he comes now to complete his redemption, he gives him one hundred and goes out:

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:10:3.hebrew: או אין נגאל - לחצאין כלל, אלא א"כ מצא כדי גאולתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:10:3.english: Or he is not redeemed - partially at all, unless he has found [enough] for his [full] redemption.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:10:4.hebrew: ואי אמרת אינו נגאל - אייקר כוליה ברשות דמריה, ויהיב ליה מאה וחמשין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:10:4.english: And if you say he cannot be redeemed partially - The whole slave became more valuable in the possession of his master, and the redeemer gives him one hundred and fifty.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:11:1.hebrew: והא אמרת נתרבה כו' - דהיכא דנשבח, אין מחשבים לו אלא כשעת מקנתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:11:1.english: But you said: "If it increased..." - For where [the slave] appreciated in value, one calculates for him only [according to his value] at the time of his purchase:

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:11:2.hebrew: דאייקר וזל ואייקר - שקנהו במאתים, והוזל ועמד על מנה, וחשיב ליה כפי שניו ונתן לו חמשים, ולא הספיק לגמור פדיונו עד שהוקר ועמד על מאתים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:11:2.english: Where he increased in value, decreased, and increased - That he bought him for two hundred, and [his value] decreased and stood at one hundred, and [the master] calculated it for him according to his [remaining] years, and [the slave] gave him fifty, and he did not manage to complete his redemption until [the slave's value] increased and stood again at two hundred.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:12:1.hebrew: ה"ג במסקנא: ואי אמרת אינו נגאל לחצאין, הני מאה פקדון נינהו גביה, יהיב ליה ניהליה ונפיק. ול"ג: והא אמרת נתמעט כספו כו'. ואי אמרת אינו נגאל לחצאין — לא קנאן האדון בתורת גאולה, ועכשיו שהכסיף הוא עומד כוליה לפדותו, והנך זוזי הוו פקדון גביה, ויהיב להו ניהליה ונפיק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:12:1.english: The correct reading in the conclusion is: "And if you say that he cannot be redeemed partially, these hundred are a deposit with him; he gives it to him and he goes out." But we do not read: "But didn't you say that his money was reduced," etc. [The meaning is:] And if you say that he cannot be redeemed partially — the master did not acquire them [the hundred] by way of redemption; and now that the slave has decreased in value, the redeemer stands to redeem all of him, and those coins are a deposit with [the master], and he gives them back to him, and the slave goes out.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:13:1.hebrew: המוכר בית בעיר חומה - שהוא נגאל עד שנה, ולא יותר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:13:1.english: One who sells a house in a walled city - For it can be redeemed until a year, and no longer.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:13:2.hebrew: נגאל לחצאין - אם נתן חצי דמיו בתוך שנה, מפריק פלגיה או לא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:13:2.english: Is redeemed in halves - If he gave half of its price within the year, does he redeem half of it, or not?

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:13:3.hebrew: שדה אחוזה - כתיב בה "ומצא כדי גאולתו", ולא לחצאין. והכא כתיב "ישיב גאולתו", ולא כתיב "כדי":
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:13:3.english: An ancestral field - Regarding it, it is written "and he finds sufficient for its redemption" (Leviticus 25:26), [implying] not in parts. But here, [regarding the Hebrew slave,] it is written "he shall return his redemption" (Leviticus 25:51), and "sufficient" is not written.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:13:4.english: Its redemption - “Its redemption shall be for a period of days” (Leviticus 25:29).

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:14:1.hebrew: היכא דגלי - התורה בכדי גאולתו, למימרא דכולה גאולה בעינן — גלי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:14:1.english: Where it revealed - [the Torah revealed] with the phrase "sufficient means for its redemption" (Leviticus 25:26), meaning that we require the entire redemption [at once] — it revealed it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:14:2.hebrew: והיכא - ובמקום דלא כתיב בה כדי, לא מייתינן ליה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:14:2.english: And where - [In a case] where "sufficient means" is not written in it, we do not bring it [into the law that it cannot be redeemed in part].

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:15:1.hebrew: שלוה - אם אין לו, לוה מאחרים וגואל. מה שאין כן מוכר בשדה אחוזה, דבעינן ״והשיגה ידו״ (ויקרא כ״ה:כ״ו). משמע נמי שגואל לחצאין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:15:1.english: One can borrow - If he does not have [the money], he borrows from others and redeems. This is unlike one who sold an ancestral field, where we require “and his hand attains” (Leviticus 25:26). It also implies that he can redeem partially.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:15:2.hebrew: ואם גאל יגאל - הכתוב במקדיש שדה אחוזה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:15:2.english: And if he will redeem [ga'ol yigal] - The verse is speaking of one who consecrates a field of inheritance.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:16:1.hebrew: לפי שמצינו כו' - ר"ש דריש טעמא דקרא בכל דוכתא (ב"מ דף קטו.), והכא נמי יהיב טעמא לקרא. ואשמעינן דהקפידה תורה לחזור, שלא תפקע אחוזה מיורשים, לפי שיפה כח מוכר, שאין נחלתו נפקעת, שהרי חוזרת לו ביובל; לפיכך לא חש ליפות כחו ללוות ולגאול לחצאין. אבל מקדיש, לפי שהורע כחו להפסיד נחלתו ביובל, כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״א) "והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל קדש" וגו' ומתחלק לכהנים, ייפה הכתוב כחו בתחלת פדיונו ללוות ולגאול לחצאין. ומהכא אית לן למיגמר נמי מוכר בית בבתי ערי חומה, דלוה וגואל וגואל לחצאין, שהרי הורע כחו ליחלט בסוף שנה ולא יצא ביובל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:16:1.english: Because we find, etc. - Rabbi Shimon expounds the reason for the verse everywhere (Bava Metzia 115a), and here too he gives a reason for the verse. And he teaches us that the Torah was particular about returning [the field], so that an ancestral field not be removed from heirs: because the power of a seller is enhanced, since his inheritance is not lost, for it returns to him in the Jubilee; therefore, [the Torah] was not concerned to enhance his power to borrow and redeem, or to redeem partially. But [regarding] one who consecrates, because his power is diminished — in that he loses his inheritance in the Jubilee, as it is written (Leviticus 27:21): "And the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy" etc., and it is divided among the priests — the verse enhanced his power at the start of his redemption, [allowing him] to borrow and redeem, and to redeem partially. And from here we must also derive [the law of] one who sells a house in the houses of walled cities, that he may borrow and redeem and redeem partially, since his power is diminished in that it becomes permanently [the buyer's] at the end of the year and does not go out in the Jubilee.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:19:1.hebrew: איתיביה - דקתני סיפא: מוכר בית בבתי ערי חומה יוכיח, שאין לוה וגואל וכו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:19:1.english: He raised an objection to him - For the latter part [of the baraita] teaches: One who sells a house in the houses of walled cities will prove [it], for he may not borrow and redeem, etc.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:1:1.hebrew: זה הנמכר לעבודת כוכבים עצמה - לחטוב עצים ושאר צרכיה, ולא לשם אלהות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:1:1.english: This is one who is sold to the idol worship itself - to chop wood and [do] its other needs, and not for the sake of divinity.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:21:1.hebrew: מוכר שדה אחוזה הורע כחו ליגאל מיד - עד שתהא שתי שנים ביד הלוקח, כדכתיב (שם כה) "במספר שני תבואות ימכר לך". אין מכירה פחותה משתי שנים מעת לעת, ואח"כ גואל בגרעון כסף, כדכתיב (שם) "לפי רוב השנים וחשב את שני ממכרו וגו'". כמה שנים הם משלקחה עד היובל שהיה עתיד להחזיר לבעלים — עשרים שנה, ודמיה עשרים מנה. הרי שקניית תבואות כל שנה במנה, וכן יגרע לכל שנה שאכלה, לפי גאולתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:21:1.english: One who sells an ancestral field — his power is diminished with regard to redeeming immediately - [He cannot redeem] until it has been in the buyer's hands for two years, as it is written (Leviticus 25): "According to the number of the years of the crops he shall sell to you." There is no sale of less than two years, [counted] from time to time; and afterward he redeems it by deducting money, as it is written (there): "According to the greater number of years... and he shall calculate the years of its sale, etc." [That is,] how many years are they from when [the buyer] took it until the Jubilee, when he was due to return it to its owners — twenty years — and its price is twenty maneh. Thus the purchase of the crops of each year is [worth] one maneh, and so he deducts for each year that [the buyer] ate [its produce], according to its redemption.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:2:1.hebrew: הא אהדריה קרא - לכל ישראל, לרחם עליו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:2:1.english: The verse brought him back - [the verse returned him] to all of Israel, to have mercy on him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:2:2.hebrew: לידחי אבן אחר הנופל - אדחה אבן, שלא תהא לו גאולה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:2:2.english: Let us throw a stone after the fallen - I will push away a stone, so that he will have no redemption.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:4:1.hebrew: רבות בשנים - משמע שיהא רבוי בשנים, וכי אפשר להיותן מרובות על שש או מועטות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:4:1.english: Many in years - This implies that there be an abundance of years; but is it possible for them to be more than six, or fewer?

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:4:2.hebrew: אלא - ה"ק: אם יש רבוי בדמיו שנתרבה בתוך שנים הללו, כגון שהשביח — "מכסף מקנתו" חשוב כמשעת קנייה, להקל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:4:2.english: Rather - This is what it means to say: If there is an increase in his value that grew during these years, for example that he improved — "out of the money that he was bought for"; he is reckoned as at the time of purchase, which is the more lenient [outcome].

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:4:3.hebrew: נתמעט כספו - בתוך שנים הללו, חשוב אותו כפי דמי שניו של עכשיו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:4:3.english: If his money decreased - Within these years, reckon him according to the value of his years at present.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:5:1.hebrew: ניתיב ליה - דמי ארבע שנים. ולא איירי קרא לא בהשביח ולא בהכסיף:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:5:1.english: Let him give him - the value of four years. And the verse does not speak either of a case where [the slave] increased in value or where [his value] decreased.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:7:1.hebrew: לחצאין - הגיע ידו לדמי חצי גרעונו, יתנם, וימעט חצי שניו מעליו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:7:1.english: In halves - If he can afford [lit., his hand reached] the price of half of his deficit [i.e., the redemption sum], he gives it, and reduces half of his years from himself.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:7:2.hebrew: או אין נגאל - כלל אלא א"כ מצא כדי גאולתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:7:2.english: Or he is not redeemed - at all, unless he has found enough [money] for his [full] redemption.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:8:1.hebrew: שדה אחוזה - כתיב בה "ומצא כדי גאולתו", ולא לחצאין. והכא כתיב "ישיב גאולתו", ולא כתיב "כדי":
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:8:1.english: An ancestral field - Concerning it, it is written, “and he finds sufficient means to redeem it,” [which implies] not in halves. But here it is written, “he shall give back his redemption,” and “sufficient” is not written.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:8:2.hebrew: או דילמא לקולא אמרינן - דגאולת חצאין יש בה להקל ולהחמיר, כדלקמיה. והיכא דהוי קולא לגביה, אמרינן דנגאל; והיכא דהוי חומרא, אמרינן דאינו נגאל, כדאמר קרא גבי השביח והכסיף, דאזלינן לקולא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:8:2.english: Or perhaps we say it for a leniency - For partial redemption has in it both leniency and stringency, as [is discussed] below. And where it is a leniency for him, we say that he is redeemed; and where it is a stringency, we say that he is not redeemed, as the verse says regarding [a slave who] improved [in value] and [whose price] rose, that we follow the lenient [side].

Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:9:1.hebrew: לאו אמרת - לעיל (קידושין דף יח.) גניבו חמש מאות ושוה אלף, לדברי הכל אינו נמכר. אלמא "ונמכר" — כולו ולא חציו משמע. הכא נמי, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ה:מ״ט) "או השיגה ידו ונגאל" — כולו ולא חציו משמע:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20b:9:1.english: Didn't you say - Earlier (Kiddushin 18a): [if] his theft was five hundred and he is worth one thousand, according to all [opinions] he is not sold. Evidently, "and he is sold" implies all of him and not half of him. Here too, as it is written (Leviticus 25:49) "or his hand attains [sufficient means] and he is redeemed" — it implies all of him and not half of him.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 20b:13:1.hebrew: גאולתו גאולתו גמר - נראה לר"ת דלאו ג"ש גמורה היא, אלא גלוי מילתא בעלמא הוא. דאי ג"ש גמורה היא, א"כ מאי קאמר "או דלמא לקולא אמרינן, לחומרא לא אמרינן"? הא כיון דהוי ג"ש, בין לקולא בין לחומרא אית לן למילף, דאין ג"ש למחצה. וכן משמע לקמיה גבי בתי ערי חומה, קאמר: היכא דגלי גלי, והיכא דלא גלי לא גלי. ואי ג"ש היא, אפילו היכא דלא גלי נמי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 20b:13:1.english: "Ge'ulato, ge'ulato" — he derives - It appears to Rabbeinu Tam that this is not a full verbal analogy (gezerah shavah), but merely a clarification of the matter. For if it were a full gezerah shavah, then what does [the Gemara] mean when it says, "Or perhaps we say it for leniency, [but] we do not say it for stringency"? Since it is a gezerah shavah, we should derive [from it] both for leniency and for stringency, for there is no such thing as a gezerah shavah [applying] in part. And so it is implied later, regarding houses in walled cities, where [the Gemara] says: Where [the Torah] revealed [a law], it is revealed, and where it did not reveal, it did not reveal. But if it were a gezerah shavah, [it would apply] even where [the Torah] did not reveal it as well:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 20b:19:1.hebrew: איתיביה - פי' מסיפא דקתני: מוכר בית בבתי ערי חומה יוכיח, שאינו לוה וגואל וגואל לחצאין. ואם תאמר: מאי פריך לרבי שמעון? דילמא הך ברייתא אתיא כוותיה דרבי שמעון, והא דקאמר לעיל גבי בתי ערי חומה שלוה וגואל וגואל לחצאין, היינו בתר דרבי לן קרא במקדיש "אם גאל יגאל"; אבל הך ברייתא דקאמר דאינו לוה וגואל וגואל לחצאין, מיירי אם לא נכתב "אם גאל יגאל", דה"נ קאמר לעיל "שיכול". וי"ל דמשמע ליה כל שיטת הברייתא אף לפי האמת לבתר דכתיב נמי "אם גאל יגאל", דאי לאו הכי אמאי נקט כל שיטה זו שאינה קיימת? הוה מצי למינקט ק"ו מע"ע: מה ע"ע שיפה כחו שיוצא ביובל, אפ"ה אינו לוה וגואל וגואל לחצאין כדבסמוך; מקדיש שהורע כחו, אם הגיע יובל אינה נגאלת ומתחלקת לכהנים, אינו דין שאין לוה וגואל וגואל לחצאין? ועל ק"ו זה ליכא למיפרך מידי. אלא פשיטא דהאי יוכיח מיירי אף לפי האמת בתר דכתב "אם גאל יגאל". וא"ת מ"מ אמאי לא נקט האי ק"ו מע"ע, כיון דליכא למיפרך מידי עילויה? וי"ל דשדה משדה עדיפא ליה למילף:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 20b:19:1.english: He raised an objection to him - Explanation: from the latter clause, where it teaches: "One who sells a house among the houses of walled cities shall prove it," [for] he may not borrow and redeem, nor redeem partially. And if you say: What is the challenge to Rabbi Shimon? Perhaps this baraita follows Rabbi Shimon, and what [the Gemara] said earlier regarding the houses of walled cities — that one may borrow and redeem, and redeem partially — that is after the verse taught us, regarding one who consecrates [a field], "And if he will redeem [ga'ol yigal]." But this baraita, which says that he may not borrow and redeem, nor redeem partially, speaks of a case where "And if he will redeem" had not been written, for so too it said earlier, "for I might have thought." And one can say that [the questioner] understands the entire line of the baraita to hold true even according to the truth, after "And if he will redeem" has also been written; for if not, why would it state this entire line of reasoning, which does not stand? It could have stated an a fortiori argument from a Hebrew slave: Just as a Hebrew slave, whose strength is superior in that he goes out in the Jubilee, nevertheless may not borrow and redeem, nor redeem partially, as [stated] immediately below; [then regarding] one who consecrates, whose strength is diminished, since if the Jubilee arrives [the field] cannot be redeemed and is divided among the priests — is it not logical that he may not borrow and redeem, nor redeem partially? And against this a fortiori argument there is nothing to challenge. Rather, it is obvious that this "shall prove it" speaks even according to the truth, after "And if he will redeem" was written. And if you ask: In any case, why did it not state this a fortiori argument from a Hebrew slave, since there is nothing to challenge about it? One can say that it preferred to derive a field from a field.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 20b:5:1.hebrew: עבד ד' ופשו ליה תרתי ניתיב ליה תרתי כפי שניו - פירש בקונטרס: לא איירי קרא לא בהשביח ולא בהכסיף. וקשה, דא"כ אמאי שני קרא בלישניה? נכתוב אידי ואידי "מכסף מקנתו" או "כפי שניו"! ואומר ה"ר ברוך דה"פ: אם עוד רבות בשנים — דעבד תרתי ופשו ליה ארבע — ליתיב ליה ארבע מכסף מקנתו, בין הכסיף ובין השביח, משום שהוא סמוך לזמן כניסה טפי מזמן יציאה. ואם מעט נשאר בשנים — דעבד ארבע ופש תרתי — ניתיב ליה כפי שניו שהוא שוה עתה, והוא סמוך לזמן יציאה, בין הכסיף ובין השביח:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 20b:5:1.english: "If he served four [years] and two remain for him, let him give him two, 'according to his years'" - Rashi explained: The verse does not speak either of the case where [the servant] increased in value or of the case where he decreased in value. But this is difficult: if so, why does the verse vary its wording? Let it write in both cases "out of the money that he was bought for" or "according to his years"! And Rabbi Baruch says that this is its meaning: "If there be yet many years" — where he served two and four remain for him — let him give him four "out of the money that he was bought for," whether [the servant] decreased in value or increased in value, because he is closer to the time of entry [into service] than to the time of exit. "And if there remain but few years" — where he served four and two remain — let him give him "according to his years," which is his value now, and he is closer to the time of exit, whether he decreased in value or increased in value:
